content:
Usually I can always go-to-definition in my editor to find where a particular command's elaborator is defined, but I don't know why this doesn't work with the syntax command. I have tried looking at the Lean source code directly, but the codebase is littered with the term syntax, and my most promissing lead, Lean.Parser.Command, doesn't seem to hold the answer.

Where can I find the definition of the syntax command? I wanted to have a closer look at how the parser infrastructure works, and thought that looking at the source code may help.

Builtin commands (and tactics, and ...) have their syntax declared in a separate file from their elaborators. Usually what I end up doing is searching in the generated docs for declarations named Lean.evalSyntax or Lean.elabSyntax, and indeed this gave me: docs#Lean.Elab.Command.elabSyntax
Yes, I was hoping to find the name of the syntax so I could find the elaborator, I didn't think of looking for the elaborator directly. Thx!

Another way to find this is to search for "syntax " in the source code. This gets you to the syntax declaration. Then you can search for the name of the syntax, «syntax», which gets you to the elaborator.
